newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo sees Namakwa Sands phase two in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Anglo sees Namakwa Sands phase two in 1999.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it expected the commissioning of the 1.2 billion rand second phase of its Namakwa Sands heavy minerals project to take place by April 1999.
Phase two involves the construction of a second ilmenite smelting furnace at Saldanha for production of titanium dioxide slag, zircon, rutile and pig iron.
The total capital investment in the project will be 2.1 billion rand.
The firm said in documents at a presentation of the group's annual report that commissioning of the northern operations will take place by October 1998 and of the smelter by April 1999.
The project life will be around 35 years and annual revenue at full production will be around one billion rand.
Production of slag will increase to 235,000 tonnes a year from 97,000, while production of pig iron is due to increase to 130,000 tonnes from 56,000.
Zircon production is to increase to 140,000 tonnes from 63,000 and that of rutile to 42,000 from 18,000.
